name: Kamat Hotels (India) Ltd
tagline: Small-cap Orchid/IRA hotel chain that has cleared its debt and pledge overhang and is finally adding keys - cheap versus peers, but with a long record of confused guidance and minority-unfriendly conduct
business_overview: Kamat Hotels operates ~19-25 hotels across brands Orchid and Toyam (premium), IRA and Lotus (mid-premium) and a few heritage properties, mainly in Maharashtra, Goa, Odisha and expanding into Tier-2 north India (Rishikesh, Dehradun, Gwalior, Ayodhya, Kutch). Most hotels are leased or managed; only Orchid Mumbai and Orchid Goa are owned. After years of aggressive debt reduction the company has cleared promoter pledges and cut finance costs sharply, and is now in a capex/key-addition phase ('Kamat 3.0', targeting 2,500 then a medium-term 4,000-5,000 keys).
fundamentals_table: TTM revenue Rs 394 Cr, net profit Rs 44 Cr, EPS ~Rs 13.6; FY26 revenue +8%, full-year profit fell (monsoon Q2)
Revenue Rs 91 Cr (+10% YoY), EBITDA Rs 25 Cr (+36%, margin 27%), PAT Rs 9.4 Cr (+158% YoY); same-store sales +17%
Borrowings ~Rs 233 Cr (Mar 2026), down from ~Rs 495 Cr (2019); promoter pledges cleared
P/E ~16, P/B ~2.15, EV/EBITDA ~9-10 - still a discount to Lemon Tree/Chalet (~18-22x) but the easy re-rating gap has narrowed
fundamentals_narrative: The balance-sheet repair is real but not fully done: borrowings are ~Rs 233 Cr (Mar 2026) vs ~Rs 495 Cr in 2019 and pledges are cleared, but this is not the ~Rs 103 Cr / near-net-cash picture the last pass implied. Operating leverage is now demonstrated across multiple quarters - Q1 FY27 same-store sales +17%, EBITDA +36% on +10% revenue, PAT +158% - with management citing >75% incremental flow-through and a 30% EBITDA-margin target over 2-3 years. The interim path is still weather-exposed (FY26 full-year profit fell on a long monsoon Q2). Valuation has re-rated (mcap Rs 529 Cr -> Rs 678 Cr, P/E ~12 -> ~16) so the deepest discount is gone, though a gap to peers remains and is the crux of the case. The recurring drag is unchanged: management refuses FY27 guidance, has a multi-year record of confused/missed guidance, several new-hotel openings (Dehradun -6 months, Nashik) are slipping, and a prior group merger was seen as minority-unfriendly. New CFO Milind Wadekar (30 yrs hospitality finance) is a positive.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Stock trades near the lower half of its 52-week band (Rs 142-369), well off the highs, roughly at/below gross block per in-thread comments.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 150 posts (Aug 2024 to Aug 2026). Trusted user ranvir (elevated) posts factual results/concall notes each quarter. The bull case (Ram_M, runitkapoor, rranjan, sanju.inlv, Wizard_apprentice; trusted RocketMan) is a valuation-plus-deleveraging-plus-key-addition re-rating story - models of 3-6x over ~1.5-2 years if occupancy recovers and the multiple converges to peers, supported by first-hand accounts of strong ARRs at Ayodhya/Pune/Rishikesh properties and an Axis credit-card rewards tie-up. The persistent bear/skeptic case (praky most vocal) is management quality: 'haven't seen a more confused management on numbers', missed/changed guidance, a CFO who fumbled a concall, the chairman skipping a concall after a miss, and an unfriendly merger - with the point that re-ratings are institution-driven and institutions distrust this name.
community_signal: ranvir (trusted, elevated) is neutral-factual. RocketMan (trusted, elevated) is mildly bullish ('4,000-5,000 keys medium term; capex finally picking up'). No trusted user has expressed strong conviction, and the loudest recurring voice (praky, non-trusted) is a management-quality skeptic. The bull thesis rests on valuation and cyclical recovery, not on management trust.
bse_notes: Promoter pledges fully released (2024). A group merger completed that some minority holders considered not minority-friendly. GOES (an investor entity) increased stake ~2% (2026). New CFO with 'rich experience' appointed. No SEBI action.
bull_case: Balance sheet fixed - pledges cleared, finance costs halved, net-debt-positive; downside is bounded
Cheapest listed hotel stock (EV/EBITDA ~8 vs peers ~20+); a re-rating to half the peer multiple alone is a multi-bagger
Key count rising ~40-50% (toward 2,500, medium-term 4,000-5,000) into a domestic-travel up-cycle, with owned-property banquet halls adding higher-margin revenue
Q1 FY27 shows the operating leverage (EBITDA +36% on +9% revenue); first-hand reports of strong ARRs and OTA commissions at new properties
bear_case: Management quality is the core problem: chronically confused and missed guidance across revenue, margin and interest cost; chairman once skipped a concall after a big miss
A group merger criticised as not minority-shareholder-friendly - a governance flag
Highly cyclical and weather-sensitive (Q2 FY26 EBITDA -62% on a long monsoon); leased/managed model means limited asset backing
Re-ratings need institutional buying, and institutions have historically avoided this name
New-property ramp depresses blended margins and ARR in the interim
verdict_headline: A de-levering small-cap hotel play with demonstrated operating leverage and a residual discount to peers - 10x-in-2-3-years at Low conviction, still gated hard by a poor management-quality record and slipping expansion timelines
verdict_reasoning: Four-box scores 2.5 with valuation=yes: at P/E ~16 / P/B ~2.15 / EV-EBITDA ~9-10 versus hospitality peers at ~18-22x, the peer-convergence re-rating is not priced in. Per the decision table, valuation=yes is the written exception that permits the 10x-in-2-3-years label at a 2.5 score, with conviction capped at Medium.

Conviction kept Low, not Medium: management still refuses FY27 guidance, the multi-year record of confused/missed guidance and a minority-unfriendly merger are unchanged, and since the last pass several new-hotel openings have slipped (Dehradun ~6 months, Nashik technical delays). No trusted user holds firm conviction.

Positives that keep it a live watch rather than 'neither': operating leverage is now proven across quarters (Q1 FY27 same-store +17%, EBITDA +36%, PAT +158%), borrowings down to ~Rs 233 Cr with pledges cleared, and an experienced new CFO.
Re-check after Q2/Q3 FY27: does occupancy hold through the monsoon quarter, do Dwarka/Gwalior actually open by end-2026, and does the 30% EBITDA-margin path show up in prints.

annual_report_findings: Borrowings ~Rs 233 Cr (Mar 2026) vs ~Rs 495 Cr (2019) - deleveraging is real but the balance sheet is not near-net-cash; the last pass's ~Rs 103 Cr figure was too low.
FY26 revenue +8% but full-year profit declined - a long monsoon Q2 remains the structural soft spot of the year.
Promoter holding 57.78%, down ~3.7% over 3 years; pledges fully released (2024); no dividend despite consistent profit.
ROCE ~15.8%, ROE ~11.6% (FY26) - clears a ~15% ROCE bar on capital employed but equity returns are still sub-14%.
5-yr sales CAGR ~42% is COVID-recovery-distorted; 3-yr profit CAGR is negative on the FY23 base effect.
quarterly_trend: Q2 FY26: weak - monsoon, occupancy dip, low/negative EBITDA
FY26 full year: revenue +8%, profit down YoY; Q4 profit +59% YoY

recent_announcements: Pipeline ~400 keys (Gwalior, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh, Mandvi); Dwarka + Gwalior guided to open by end-2026.
Dehradun opening delayed ~6 months (owner-side); Nashik faces technical delays that may push it past the Kumbh window.
New CFO Milind Wadekar (30+ yrs hospitality finance) appointed.
Management declined to give specific FY27 financial guidance, citing uncertainty; reiterated a 30% EBITDA-margin aspiration over 2-3 years.
key_new_facts: Operating leverage is now demonstrated, not hypothetical - two consecutive Q1s of triple-digit PAT growth and same-store sales +17%.
Debt is higher than the last pass recorded (~Rs 233 Cr, not ~Rs 103 Cr) - deleveraging continues but isn't finished.
Expansion timeline is slipping - a concrete, recurring instance of the execution-credibility concern.
Valuation has re-rated ~30% since the last pass; the deepest discount is gone though a peer gap remains.
open_questions: Does occupancy hold through Q2 FY27 (monsoon), or does the seasonal collapse repeat?
Will Dwarka/Gwalior actually open by end-2026, and how quickly do they ramp?
Can EBITDA margin move toward 30% while new-property ramp costs are in the base?
Is the residual ~Rs 233 Cr debt on a clear glide path to zero?
deep_dive.conviction_update: Low -> Low. Operating leverage and deleveraging strengthen the case, but management still won't guide, expansion timelines have slipped since the last pass, and the valuation discount has partly closed. Four-box holds at 2.5 (valuation=yes exception) so the 10x label stays; conviction stays Low on the unchanged management-quality gate.

No dividend despite consistent profit. A prior group merger was viewed by some minority holders as not minority-friendly.

track_record.note: FY22-FY26 checked for revenue growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% in the same year. FY23 (post-COVID recovery) and FY25 (revenue +19%, ROCE ~15.8%) plausibly cleared both; FY22 was COVID-depressed, FY24 ROCE was borderline, FY26 revenue grew only ~8%. History is real but cyclically distorted by the pandemic.
